ITEMS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT RECORDED HERE - the player's rule, 2026-08-29: an item is chosen only once the six Pokemon of a team are fixed, never per build. With ~30 trained Pokemon and the Item Clause forbidding duplicates, arguing items build-by-build is wasted work. Mega Stones are the one exception and live in the 'mega' field, because the stone is what creates the form. Validate with: python scripts/query.py build A BUILD BELONGS TO THE POKEMON, NOT TO A TEAM. Anything trained here can be reused in any team; teams.json references these rather than repeating them. A 'status' field may mention where it was tested, but that is history, not ownership.

_sp_rules.note: Confirmed across all 84 Smogon VGC spreads and every pokebase team spread: they sum to exactly 66.

training_cost_vp._note: Observed in-game 2026-08-29. Serebii still lists launch prices (2/100/200/400) and is wrong.

_sp_rules.sp_to_stat_ratio: 1 SP = 1 point of the final stat. Verified across all 84 pokebase speed tiers: every one has maxNeutral - 0Neutral == 32, the SP cap. So an uninvested stat plus the SP spent is the final number.
_sp_rules.stat_formula: Final stat = floor((base + 20 + SP) * nature), where nature is 1.1 / 1.0 / 0.9. Verified against all 84 pokebase speed tiers: 0-neutral is always base+20, max-neutral always base+52 (the 32 SP cap), max-positive always floor(max-neutral * 1.1) and 0-negative always floor(0-neutral * 0.9). WATCH OUT: pokebase's 'max neutral' column is NOT what a Timid or Jolly build reaches - that is the 'max+' column.

builds.role: Trick Room special attacker
builds.rationale: Turns a bad Speed stat into an asset under Trick Room. Quiet raises Sp. Atk and lowers Speed; 0 SP in Speed keeps it as slow as possible. Eelevate gives Ground immunity and raises its highest stat on a KO. Off-meta on purpose: 0 of 395 Worlds teams ran Eelektross, so nobody prepares for it.
builds.status: climbed to Master Rank 3 with this
builds.mega_note: The stone pays for damage and costs the Trick Room premise. Gained: SpA 105 -> 135, Atk 115 -> 145, BST 515 -> 615, and Eelevate, which keeps everything Levitate did (immune to Ground, Spikes, Toxic Spikes and Sticky Web) and adds +1 to the highest stat on a KO - so nothing is given up on the ability side, unusually. Given up: slowness. Speed 50 -> 80. Under Trick Room the slower Pokemon moves first, so the Mega acts 30 points LATER in the turn order than the base form, against a build whose whole spread is tuned to be as slow as possible. Un-mega'd it keeps 105 SpA and the better Trick Room speed. Mega Evolve when the extra 30 SpA matters more than moving first, not by default.

builds.role: Armor Tail support / Trick Room setter
builds.rationale: Brought for Armor Tail, not for Trick Room: it blanks Prankster-boosted status (Whimsicott's Encore and Tailwind, on ~24% of Worlds teams) and Fake Out, making the opening turns safe. Twin Beam hits twice, so it breaks Focus Sash - Smogon lists it as the way to OHKO Sash Glimmora and Sneasler.
builds.follows: Smogon VGC26 Regulation M-A, Trick Room Support, offensive spread
builds._moveset_corrected: CORRECTED BY THE PLAYER 2026-09-06: the recorded set (Twin Beam / Thunderbolt / Protect / Trick Room) was stale. The Pokemon as actually trained is PSYCHIC / IMPRISON / TRICK ROOM / PROTECT - it was finished on the Mega Glalie team and left that way. This is the set the player described as 'impecable' and 'bien molesta'.
builds.imprison_note: IMPRISON is the reason this set is shaped the way it is. Smogon's mechanic text: 'No foe can use any move known by the user' - it hits FOES only, so allies keep their own copies. With Psychic / Imprison / Trick Room / Protect on the user, an active Imprison denies the opposing side PROTECT, TRICK ROOM and PSYCHIC at once. Protect is the one that matters most: 69.7% of all Worlds slots carry it, so Imprison turns off the single most common move in the format for the opponent while this team keeps its own five Protects. Trick Room being sealed is the second half - the opponent cannot flip the room off, which is the exact failure mode a fully-committed TR team has. Cost: it is one turn, and Farigiraf can only set one of Imprison or Trick Room per turn.
builds._spread_corrected: CORRECTED BY THE PLAYER 2026-09-06. The file had Smogon's OFFENSIVE spread (12 HP / 24 Def / 27 SpA / 3 SpD, Modest). The player runs Smogon's PHYSICALLY DEFENSIVE spread, 30 HP / 24 Def / 12 SpD - the one whose stated benchmark is surviving BLACK GLASSES Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave. VERIFIED with Smogon's own engine: 83.6-99.6%, it survives by a hair. The offensive spread this file used to record takes 99.5-118.8% from the same hit and DIES on most rolls, so the player's choice is right and the record was wrong. Nature is Bold (+Def, -Atk) or RELAXED (+Def, -Spe) - see nature_note.
builds.nature_note: Smogon pairs a -Speed nature with each spread: 'A Relaxed, Quiet, or Sassy nature can be used over a Bold, Modest, or Calm nature, respectively, if you want Farigiraf to outspeed neutral-natured base 60s like Sylveon and Incineroar under Trick Room.' For THIS spread the Trick Room nature is RELAXED, not Quiet - Quiet belongs to the offensive spread. Relaxed keeps the identical Defense and drops Speed 80 -> 72, which under Trick Room moves Farigiraf ahead of Incineroar (41.4% of teams) and Sylveon (24.9%). Trick Room is priority -7, so Speed never matters on the turn the room goes up. Cost 500 VP or one free training ticket.
builds.damage_note: At 0 Sp. Atk investment Psychic is still a GUARANTEED OHKO on Sneasler (153.3-182.0%), which is the job Smogon gives it. It no longer threatens Mega Staraptor (67.4-81.4%) or Venusaur (64.7-76.6%) - those were numbers from the offensive spread and do not apply here. This Farigiraf is pure support.

builds.role: Physical Sharpness attacker / Spikes setter
builds.rationale: Sharpness raises Slicing moves by 50%, and three of the four qualify: Razor Shell 75 -> 112.5 and Ceaseless Edge 65 -> 97.5 both with STAB, Sacred Sword 90 -> 135 unresisted coverage that ignores the target's stat changes. Sucker Punch is not Slicing, so it stays at 70 STAB, but it is the only priority on the set. Ceaseless Edge sets Spikes on hit, so pressure accumulates even on a resisted hit. Max Speed neutral reaches 137, the top of speed tier 85; Adamant keeps Attack maxed instead of trading into 150.
builds.meta_note: Worlds: 5 of 395 teams, Sharpness 100%, Sacred Sword 100%, Razor Shell 80%. Pikalytics championtournaments: 48.4% win rate (123-131); Sacred Sword 77.9%, Ceaseless Edge 61.0%, Sucker Punch 59.7%. The player's four moves are all in the common pool; the usual Worlds pick is Jolly 60% over Adamant 20%, and Flip Turn 80% / Night Slash 100% instead of Ceaseless Edge + Sucker Punch.
builds.playstyle_note: Physical main attacker, so it is exposed to Intimidate (Incineroar is on ~41% of Worlds teams). The player trained it this way; flagged only because their standing preference is special main attackers.

builds.role: Setup sweeper (Bulk Up + recovery)
builds.rationale: Bulk Up raises Attack and Defense together, and Bitter Blade heals 1/2 of the damage it deals, so every boosted turn pays for the chip taken while setting up. Shadow Sneak is priority for Focus Sash users and low-HP targets that would otherwise move first (Sneasler, Kingambit). Flash Fire is not filler: it walls Mega Charizard Y outright and, under its sun, feeds an even stronger Bitter Blade.
builds.follows: Smogon VGC26 Regulation M-A and M-B, Setup Sweeper - moves, ability, nature and the exact SP spread all match the published set. Smogon on this spread: it survives Stomping Tantrum from Jolly Garchomp and +2 Kowtow Cleave from Black Glasses Kingambit while at +1 Def from Bulk Up, gives the best odds of surviving Mega Gengar's Shadow Ball, and the Attack SPs OHKO no-bulk Basculegion-M with +2 Shadow Sneak and nearly always OHKO Kingambit with +1 Bitter Blade.
builds.meta_note: Worlds: 3 of 395 teams, and all three ran exactly these four moves with Flash Fire and Colbur Berry 100%. Pikalytics championtournaments: 46.4% win rate over 2448 games; Bitter Blade 99.6%, Shadow Sneak 94.7%, Protect 92.4%, Bulk Up 82.2%. This is the standard set, not a variant.
builds.threats: Resisted by Incineroar, Hydreigon and Mega Tyranitar, which answer back with Throat Chop / Dark Pulse / Knock Off. Garchomp shrugs off both attacks and threatens Earthquake and Stomping Tantrum. Basculegion-M OHKOes with Last Respects or Wave Crash even through a Bulk Up. Rock-types (Hisuian Arcanine, Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Tyranitar) resist Bitter Blade and click Rock Slide.

builds.role: Snow setter / Aurora Veil + Contrary-ally install
builds.rationale: Snow Warning is the engine for the whole set: it makes Blizzard never miss (110 BP, 70 accuracy otherwise, and it is a spread move in doubles) and it is the precondition for Aurora Veil, which cannot be used outside snow. Timid with 32 Speed SP reaches 177, ahead of everything in the box except Aerodactyl and Jolteon. Charm replaces Smogon's Encore: -2 Attack is two Intimidates in one move with 20 PP, and on a Contrary ally it is +2 Attack instead.
builds.deviation_from_smogon: Smogon's Offensive Support set is Blizzard / Aurora Veil / Encore / Protect with this exact spread, nature and ability. The player runs Charm over Encore. Charm does not appear in the Worlds move splits or in Pikalytics' top eight, so it is an off-meta call. Trade: Encore punishes Fake Out and setup (Kingambit's Swords Dance, Mega Aerodactyl's Tailwind) by locking the move; Charm does nothing against a special attacker or a status move, but it holds a physical threat down for far longer than one turn and stacks with Aurora Veil's physical reduction. RESOLVED: the player's actual use was offensive, not defensive - Charm is the setup button for a Contrary ally. Against a foe it still functions as a double Intimidate, but that is the secondary mode.
builds.meta_note: Worlds: 17 of 395 teams (4.3%), Snow Warning 100%, Timid 82%. Ladder 5.7%. Pikalytics championtournaments 48.1% win rate over 4234 games; Blizzard 96.0%, Protect 81.8%, Aurora Veil 34.7%. The tournament build leans Freeze-Dry + Encore + Icy Wind on a Choice Scarf; the player's is the Veil build instead.
builds.threats: Fire-types (Incineroar's Flare Blitz, Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave) and Rock-types (Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Tyranitar, Lycanroc-D with Rock Slide). Any rival weather setter turns off the snow, which costs both Blizzard's accuracy and Aurora Veil at once. Kingambit and Archaludon OHKO through the Veil with Iron Head and Flash Cannon. Sneasler and Mega Gengar outspeed it.
builds.team_note: ANTI-SYNERGY with the player's own Farigiraf: Trick Room turns this 177 Speed into a liability, and Smogon lists Trick Room Farigiraf as a check to Alolan Ninetales by name. These two belong to different teams, or Trick Room stays unclicked in the games Ninetales is brought.
builds.charm_combo: CONFIRMED BY THE PLAYER: Charm was aimed at their OWN Mega Staraptor, not at a foe. Mega Staraptor's only ability is Contrary, whose text reads 'moves that lower the stats raise the stat', and Charm is unambiguously a move, so Charm's -2 Attack becomes +2 Attack on the ally. Charm's target field is 'Selected Target', so it can legally pick the partner in doubles. Ninetales at 177 Speed moves first and installs the turn: Aurora Veil up, partner at +2. 20 PP means it can be repeated. Note this does not depend on the open question of whether Contrary inverts Intimidate, since that is an ability rather than a move.
builds.build_constraint: Three of the four moves are status, so a Choice item can never go on this build - it would lock Ninetales into Charm, Aurora Veil or Protect. Worth remembering because the Worlds Alolan Ninetales runs Choice Scarf 65%, but that is the Freeze-Dry / Icy Wind / Encore build, not this one.

builds.role: Mega special sweeper under its own snow
builds.rationale: Mega Evolution is what makes the set work: SpA 80 -> 140, Spe 110 -> 120, and Snow Warning arrives, which makes Blizzard never miss. Blizzard hits All Adjacent Foes, so a Nasty Plot turn (+2 SpA) turns it into a spread nuke off 140 base with no accuracy risk. Ghost typing means Fake Out cannot stop the setup turn. Snow also raises the Defense of Ice-types, so the setup turn is protected from both sides.
builds.deviation_from_smogon: Smogon and the field run this as an Aurora Veil Setter: Blizzard / Shadow Ball / Aurora Veil / Protect. The player runs Nasty Plot over Aurora Veil - 5% of Worlds Froslass, against 55% on Aurora Veil. That converts it from a support Mega into a standalone special sweeper, which fits the player's preference for special main attackers. It is defensible here because the team's Aurora Veil already lives on Ninetales-Alola.
builds.mega_timing: Smogon's timing note, worth keeping: Froslass does NOT have to Mega Evolve on turn 1. Held in base form it keeps Cursed Body (30% to disable a move that hits it), which punishes Rock Slide from Aerodactyl, and it can Mega Evolve later to overwrite a slower weather setter's weather (Mega Charizard Y, Pelipper, Mega Tyranitar) at the moment the snow is actually needed.
builds.meta_note: Worlds: 20 of 395 teams (5.1%), Froslassite 100%, Cursed Body 100%, Timid 70%. Blizzard 100%, Protect 100%, Shadow Ball 95%, Aurora Veil 55%, Nasty Plot 5%. Ladder 5.8%. Speed tier 110 -> 162 at max neutral before Mega; Mega Froslass is base 120.
builds.threats: Anything that removes the snow: Mega Charizard Y's Drought, Mega Tyranitar's sand. Hisuian Arcanine OHKOes through snow's Defense boost with Head Smash or Flare Blitz. Kingambit and Incineroar wall both STAB moves and hit back; Kingambit's Sucker Punch picks it off once chipped. Archaludon eats Blizzard and answers with Flash Cannon. Aerodactyl outspeeds and clicks Rock Slide.
builds.mega_note: Mega-dependent: Snow Warning, the 140 Sp. Atk and the never-missing Blizzard all arrive with the stone. Un-mega'd it keeps Cursed Body and 80 Sp. Atk, which is a different Pokemon. Bring the stone if this one is meant to attack.

builds.role: Bulky setup sweeper behind a status immunity
builds.rationale: Steel/Ghost with Good as Gold - full immunity to other Pokemon's status moves - is what buys the Nasty Plot turn: no Encore, no Taunt, no Thunder Wave, no Will-O-Wisp, no Parting Shot can touch it. Same job Armor Tail does for Farigiraf, but self-only and not limited to Prankster. Make It Rain is 120 BP and hits All Adjacent Foes; Shadow Ball is the single-target answer to Basculegion-M.
builds.moveset_note: Re-studied against the real threat list 2026-09-01 and KEPT UNCHANGED. The two attacks are both team-critical and neither is replaceable. MAKE IT RAIN answers the Fairy core - Whimsicott 38.9%, Sylveon 33.3%, Mega Floette 27.8% of Worlds Masters teams - and Fairy is Mega Chesnaught's x2. SHADOW BALL answers the Ghosts: Basculegion 95-112% and Sinistcha 98-116%, both roll OHKOs, and Ghost is the type nothing on this team resists. NASTY PLOT is what turns Sylveon and Mega Floette from 2HKOs into OHKOs. MAKE IT RAIN OVER FLASH CANNON, decided on numbers: Flash Cannon costs no Sp. Atk and has 12 PP to Make It Rain's 8, but at +2 Make It Rain GUARANTEES three KOs that Flash Cannon only rolls - Garchomp (102-121% vs 92-108%), Farigiraf (105-125% vs 94-111%) and Sinistcha (109-129% vs 98-116%) - and it is a spread move, hitting both foes. The -2 Sp. Atk afterwards is the price, and it is why this is a burst and not a spam button: fire it at +2, then Shadow Ball at +0 still rolls a KO on Basculegion and Sinistcha. REJECTED: Focus Blast OHKOes Kingambit (162-191%) but 70 accuracy and Mega Chesnaught's Body Press already OHKOes it at 144-171% guaranteed. Power Gem OHKOes Mega Charizard Y (115-136%) but Rotom-Wash and Chesnaught's Rock Slide both cover it. Psychic OHKOes Sneasler (170-201%) but Gholdengo is already immune to Sneasler's entire moveset. Steel Beam costs 50% max HP and is on 0 of 395 Masters teams. Surf hits the ally. Recover is a real option for a Trick Room sweeper but there is no slot: all four are load-bearing.
builds.deviation_from_smogon: Moves, ability and role match the standard set exactly (Worlds: Make It Rain 100%, Shadow Ball 100%, Protect 100%, Nasty Plot 65%). The spread differs. Smogon's bulky spread is 32 HP / 8 Def / 7 SpA / 3 SpD / 16 Spe with Timid; the player keeps the identical defensive shell (32 HP / 8 Def / 3 SpD) but moves the 16 Speed and the spare SP into 23 SpA and runs Modest. So Smogon's defensive benchmarks still hold - almost always survives Earthquake from Jolly Life Orb Garchomp, withstands Dark Pulse from Mega Blastoise - but the Speed benchmark does NOT: this Gholdengo sits at 104 Speed and does not outspeed Adamant Basculegion-M. It is the slower, harder-hitting reading of the same shell.
builds.meta_note: Worlds: 23 of 395 teams (5.8%), Good as Gold 100%, Modest 74%, Life Orb 78%. Ladder 9.8%, the highest of any Pokemon recorded here so far. Pikalytics championtournaments 48.4% win rate over 7341 games. NOTE: Staraptor appears as a partner on 100% of the 23 Worlds teams that ran Gholdengo - the player already owns that pairing.
builds.spread_note: Quiet 32 HP / 8 Def / 23 SpA / 3 SpD, RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-01 against the KO-count rule and kept unchanged. HP 32 + Def 8 is the EXACT minimum that survives Kingambit Kowtow Cleave (84-99%; at 32 HP / 0 Def it is 88-105%, a roll KO). Kingambit is on 88.9% of the top-18 Worlds teams, so this one threshold justifies the 40 points. SpA 23 rather than 32 costs almost nothing: across 12 meta targets the only KO category that changes is Shadow Ball on Sinistcha (roll 98-116% -> guaranteed 104-122%), and AFTER Nasty Plot not a single category differs between 23 and 32 - every threshold is already crossed at 23. More defence is not worth buying: nothing reaches a real survival threshold. Incineroar Flare Blitz needs Def 16 just to leave guaranteed-OHKO range (97-116%, still dies on most rolls) and that does not fit alongside HP 32 and SpA 23; Mega Charizard Y Heat Wave in sun OHKOes through even 32 HP / 32 SpD (102-121%). Those two matchups are unwinnable with SP and must be answered by the team - Rotom-Wash covers both. NATURE CHANGED Modest -> Quiet 2026-09-01 for the Trick Room team. Quiet raises Sp. Atk by the same x1.1, so every damage number above is UNCHANGED (SpA 193); it lowers Speed instead of the unused Attack, 104 -> 93. That fixes the flaw this build already recorded: at 104 it did not outspeed Adamant Basculegion-M (98), and under Trick Room 93 moves BEFORE it. Costs 500 VP; no SP change.

builds.role: Fast Tailwind setter / spread flincher
builds.rationale: Base 130 Speed with Jolly and 32 SP is 200 - floor((130+20+32)*1.1) - the fastest thing in the player's box, tied with Jolteon. Tailwind therefore lands before almost anything can stop it, and Rock Slide's 30% flinch is applied first. Rock Slide targets All Adjacent Foes. Unnerve is the quiet part: while Aerodactyl is on the field NO opposing Pokemon can eat its held Berry, which switches off Kingambit's Chople and Occa Berries, Ceruledge's Colbur, and Sitrus Berry generally - the single most contested item in the format at 309 Worlds teams.
builds.follows: Smogon VGC26 Regulation M-A, Focus Sash Offensive Support - moves, ability, nature and the exact SP spread all match. It is also, move for move, the highest-placing Aerodactyl at Worlds: #11 Naoto Mizobuchi [JP], 7-1, Focus Sash / Unnerve / Jolly / Rock Slide / Dual Wingbeat / Tailwind / Protect.
builds.meta_note: Worlds: 39 of 395 teams (9.9%), Unnerve 100%, Jolly 92%. Ladder 12.8%. IMPORTANT: 85% of those ran Aerodactylite, which the player does NOT own (2000 VP in the shop). The other 15% ran Focus Sash, and on the tournament ladder Pikalytics has Focus Sash at 88.6%. So the non-Mega build is a real, supported build, not a fallback - but every Smogon and Worlds reference to Mega Aerodactyl outspeeding, or to Tough Claws, does not apply to this one.
builds.mega_note: This build does not want the Mega, and the stone is not owned anyway (2000 VP). Mega Aerodactyl trades Unnerve for Tough Claws, and Unnerve is the entire point of this set: while it is on the field no opponent can eat a held Berry, which switches off Kingambit's Chople and Occa, Ceruledge's Colbur and every Sitrus Berry in the format. Tough Claws would boost only Dual Wingbeat here, because Rock Slide is not a contact move. The Mega does add Speed 130 -> 150 and Attack 105 -> 135, so it is a real attacker - just a different Pokemon from this one. If the stone is ever bought, build it as a second Aerodactyl rather than converting this one.

builds.role: Bulky attacker / Intimidate punisher
builds.rationale: Kowtow Cleave NEVER MISSES (accuracy 101 in the Champions movedex), so the main STAB has no variance at all. Sucker Punch is priority +1 for anything faster that has committed to attacking. Defiant makes an Intimidate lead a mistake: +2 Attack the moment the opponent lowers a stat, and it is live from entry rather than on Mega Evolution. 0 Speed SP on base 50 leaves it at 70, which is where it wants to be if Trick Room is ever up.
builds.follows: Smogon VGC26 Regulation M-A and M-B, Bulky Attacker - exact match on moves, ability, nature and the SP spread 32 HP / 32 Atk / 2 Def. Smogon lists the third slot as Iron Head / Low Kick; the player took Iron Head.
builds.ability_note: DEFIANT'S CHAMPIONS TEXT MATTERS FOR THIS BOX: 'Attack is raised by two stages when the Pokemon has its stats lowered. Doesn't work on self inflicted stat drops or drops from ALLIES.' So Charm from the player's own Ninetales-Alola will NOT trigger Defiant - the Charm install works on Mega Staraptor's Contrary and on nothing else in the box.
builds.meta_note: THE most used Pokemon in the format: 208 of 395 Worlds teams (52.7%) and 34.4% of the ladder, Defiant 100%, Adamant 88%. Pikalytics 51.4% win rate over 25582 games - one of the few above 50%. The Worlds winner (YUYA WAKASUGI [JP], 8-0-0) ran Kingambit with Chople Berry and Low Kick in place of Protect. builds.form_note: Male form - the DB key 'Basculegion' is the male (120/112/65/80/75/78). Basculegion-Female is a separate form with the special split.
builds.role: Trick Room priority finisher - Adaptability Aqua Jet, unconditional
builds.rationale: Adaptability turns STAB from x1.5 into x2, and both STABs are the point. Last Respects starts at 50 BP and gains 50 for every fainted ally, so it scales from filler to a 200 BP nuke as the game goes; at x2 STAB that is the highest ceiling in the box. Wave Crash is 120 BP for 1/3 recoil, and Aqua Jet is the +1 priority finisher. Protect over Flip Turn keeps it on the field, which is what Last Respects wants.
builds.follows: The Worlds winner's set, exactly: YUYA WAKASUGI [JP], 8-0-0, #1 - Basculegion [Male] @ Life Orb, Adaptability, Adamant, Wave Crash / Last Respects / Aqua Jet / Protect. Smogon's published set is different (Choice Scarf Revenge Killer with Flip Turn over Protect, 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe).
builds.spread_note: Brave 16 HP / 24 Atk / 8 Def / 18 SpD, converted to Trick Room 2026-09-02. NATURE: Brave, not Adamant. Both raise Attack by the same x1.1 - Atk 171 either way - so Brave is a free 30 points of Speed dropped (118 -> 88) by lowering the unused Sp. Atk slot's counterpart instead. Same trick as Quiet over Modest on Gholdengo and Rotom-Wash. SPEED 0 always on this team. THE 20 POINTS FREED FROM SPEED went to Def and SpD and bought three category flips: Def 6 -> 8 is the exact threshold for Kingambit's Sucker Punch (85-100%, dies on the max roll -> 82-98%, survives) and Kingambit is on 52.7% of Worlds Masters teams; SpD 0 -> 18 flips Mega Froslass Shadow Ball (88-103% -> 72-86%) and Archaludon Electro Shot (95-112% -> 81-95%). NOT BOUGHT: Mega Gengar's Shadow Ball needs a full 20 SpD (82-98%) and that only fits by dropping Def below the Sucker Punch threshold - Gengar is 5.8% of teams against Kingambit's 52.7%, so the trade is clear. ATK KEPT AT 24 rather than 32: the 8 extra points only flip Wave Crash on Incineroar from a 95-113% roll KO to a guaranteed one and Last Respects on Sinistcha to a roll, which is not worth surrendering the Froslass and Archaludon benchmarks.
builds.meta_note: Worlds: 134 of 395 teams (33.9%), Adaptability 100%, Adamant 70%. Ladder 28.0%. Pikalytics 50.8% win rate over 18899 games. Core: Basculegion + Kingambit, 1619 teams (12.3%) - the second most common core recorded, and Kingambit is its top partner at 79%.
builds.build_constraint: Wave Crash already costs 1/3 of the damage dealt as recoil, so any HP-draining item stacks a second source of self-damage onto a build whose Last Respects wants it to stay on the field.
builds.moveset_note: Unchanged - this is exactly Smogon's [Bulky Attacker] set and it needs no adaptation for Trick Room, because priority works identically inside and outside it. AQUA JET is why this Pokemon is on the team: Adaptability doubles STAB instead of the usual x1.5, so 40 BP becomes 80 EFFECTIVE with NO condition attached - the best unconditional priority the player owns, and the team had none at all. Smogon also notes it 'allows Basculegion-M to potentially evade Kingambit's Sucker Punch'. WAVE CRASH is the main STAB and OHKOes Sneasler. LAST RESPECTS scales +50 BP per fallen ally and is the late-game sweep button - but note it does ZERO to Normal-types, so an opposing Farigiraf is immune. PROTECT is the standard slot. Smogon's other two sets are rejected on the player's own rules: the [Revenge Killer] needs a Choice Scarf (vetoed - no move-locking items) and the [Focus Sash Attacker] swaps to Liquidation, which loses the Sneasler OHKO.
builds.threats: Immune to Fighting (Sneasler Close Combat does 0%) and to Normal. Weak to Electric, Grass, Ghost and Dark. Smogon: 'Priority attackers pose the biggest threat to Basculegion-M. Kingambit is at the forefront' - the Def 8 threshold above is built for exactly that. Mega Gengar still OHKOes it with Shadow Ball on a high roll; that matchup is played around, not built for. NOTE Smogon designs this Pokemon as an ANTI-Trick Room revenge killer ('Wave Crash lets it threaten Trick Room setters such as Farigiraf, as Basculegion-M's bulk usually isn't enough to outlast Trick Room'), so this build deliberately departs from its intended role - what carries over is the priority, which is field-effect agnostic.

builds.role: Fast physical attacker with double spread coverage
builds.rationale: Two spread moves on one Pokemon: Earthquake at 100 BP and Rock Slide at 75 BP with a 30% flinch. Jolly with 32 Speed SP reaches 169 off base 102. Leading un-mega'd applies Intimidate to both opponents on entry; Mega Evolving instead turns every incoming Intimidate into +1 Attack. builds.contrary_confirmed: FULLY ANSWERED BY THE PLAYER IN GAME, 2026-08-29. builds.moveset_note: Studied against the real threat list 2026-09-01. THUNDERBOLT is the team's Basculegion answer (95-112% roll OHKO) and also rolls Mega Charizard Y (86-102%) and Mega Aerodactyl (98-117%). Discharge was cut: it is 'All Adjacent Pokemon' and damages the ally - fine on the Mega Sceptile team where Lightning Rod absorbs it, dead here. HYDRO PUMP stays despite 80 accuracy - it is the ONLY Water attack Rotom-Wash learns, it is the team's only Incineroar answer (96-114% roll OHKO) and it OHKOes Mega Aerodactyl (120-143%). Note it is halved under Charizard's Drought, so Thunderbolt is the reliable line into sun. WILL-O-WISP over Shadow Ball, the biggest finding of the study: Shadow Ball scored no KO anywhere (Basculegion 56-67%, Sinistcha 58-70%) and both targets are already covered - Thunderbolt kills Basculegion, Gholdengo's own Shadow Ball kills Sinistcha. Will-O-Wisp instead flipped SEVEN of seven physical matchups tested: Kingambit Kowtow Cleave on Gholdengo 2HKO -> 3HKO, Basculegion Last Respects on Gholdengo 1HKO -> 2HKO, Wave Crash 2HKO -> 3HKO, Sneasler Close Combat 2HKO -> 3HKO, Garchomp Earthquake 2HKO -> 3HKO, Mega Aerodactyl Dual Wingbeat on Chesnaught 2HKO -> 4HKO. Kingambit alone is 88.9% of the top-18 Worlds teams. LIMITS: 85 accuracy, and Fire-types CANNOT be burned, so it does nothing to Incineroar (41.3%) or Charizard (38.9%) - those two are Hydro Pump's and Thunderbolt's job. REJECTED: Thunder Wave and Electroweb both lower the target's Speed, which under Trick Room makes the opponent move EARLIER - they are anti-synergy with this team, and Electroweb is on 0 of 395 Masters teams. Hyper Voice does ZERO to Basculegion and Sinistcha (Normal vs Ghost). Thunder outdamages Thunderbolt and OHKOes Basculegion (115-136%) but 70 accuracy without rain is not worth the whiff.
builds.spread_note: Quiet 32 HP / 18 SpD / 16 SpA, corrected 2026-09-01 (player caught the error: Solar Beam is a SPECIAL move, so the stat that answers it is Special Defense - an earlier version of this spread put the points in Defense and did not survive it). PRINCIPLE: the spread is aimed at Trick Room - Speed 0 always, so it is fast under TR - but the leftover points buy survival for when TR is down or Farigiraf has died, because outside TR this sits at 95 Speed and eats the hit first. NATURE: Quiet, not Modest. Both raise Sp. Atk x1.1 so damage is identical; Quiet drops Speed instead of the unused Attack. THE 16 POINTS MOVED FROM SPA TO SPD buy the one category flip that matters: Mega Charizard Y Solar Beam 1HKO (96-113%) -> 2HKO (84-99%). Solar Beam is the ONLY attack in the format that OHKOes this Rotom-Wash, it is on 58/395 Masters teams, and 18 SpD is the exact minimum (HP 20/SpD 30, 24/26 and 28/22 all reach the same 84-99%, so 32 HP is taken because raw HP also helps against physical attacks). It also improves Mega Floette Light of Ruin 82-98% -> 71-85% and Sinistcha Matcha Gotcha 78-93% -> 69-82%. COST: Thunderbolt stops being a roll KO on Mega Charizard Y (86-102% -> 76-92%), affordable because Chesnaught's Rock Slide already rolls it (89-105%) and Hydro Pump OHKOes it out of sun. The 2 points that used to sit in Def were buying nothing - dropping them changes no category (Kowtow Cleave 48-58% -> 50-59%, Last Respects 66-80% -> 69-81%, both still 2HKO). SPA 16 is the exact floor for the three KOs that are this Pokemon's job: Thunderbolt roll-KO on Basculegion (86-102%), Hydro Pump roll-KO on Incineroar (87-104%), Hydro Pump OHKO on Mega Aerodactyl (108-129%). REJECTED Smogon's Bold 31/12/1/20/2: it reaches the same Solar Beam benchmark but 1 SpA collapses the offence to zero KOs, deleting this Pokemon's job here.
builds.threats: Survives everything relevant at 0 HP investment, which is why the spread is fully offensive: Mega Charizard Y Heat Wave in sun 42-50%, Basculegion Wave Crash 49-58%, Kingambit Kowtow Cleave 61-73%, Sneasler Close Combat 76-91%, Sylveon Hyper Voice 28-34%. Levitate makes it immune to Ground, which is Gholdengo's x2 - that is half the reason it is on this team.

builds.spread_note: Sassy 32 HP / 32 SpD / 2 Def, chosen by the player's KO-count rule: SP only count if they change a 1HKO into a 2HKO. Pays for: Mega Charizard Y Heat Wave IN SUN (OHKO 127-151% -> 2HKO 78-92%) - Charizard is on 45% of Masters teams and this single matchup justifies the whole spread; Scovillain Overheat (OHKO -> 74-87%); Floette Moonblast (roll -> 60-71%); Floette Light of Ruin partially (OHKO -> 86-103%). builds.moveset_note: Rock Slide over Knock Off (player, 2026-09-01). Knock Off's Dark damage was redundant: Body Press already OHKOes Kingambit (144-171%, and Knock Off did 12-14% there), and Gholdengo's Shadow Ball OHKOes every Ghost Knock Off was covering - Basculegion 95-112%, Mega Froslass 101-120%, Sinistcha 119-141%. Rock Slide buys what the team did not have: a roll OHKO on Mega Charizard Y (89-105% at 0 Atk SP, x4), which is the team's only weakness with zero resists, and it answers FLYING, this Pokemon's own x4 structural hole. It is 'All Adjacent Foes', so it never touches the ally - unlike Earthquake and Bulldoze, the only other physical spread moves Chesnaught learns, which would hit Gholdengo (Ground x2, 37-44% of friendly fire). Bulldoze is additionally dead: 0 of 395 Worlds teams run it, and its -1 Speed works against Trick Room. WHAT IS GIVEN UP: this removes the team's only item removal (Focus Sash 339 Worlds teams, Sitrus 309, Life Orb 273), and Farigiraf coverage drops from Knock Off's 66-78% to Body Press's 50-59%. Shadow Claw was disqualified earlier: Ghost does ZERO to Farigiraf and gains nothing over Dark. Payback is dead - it doubles only when moving AFTER the target, and under Trick Room this Pokemon moves FIRST. builds.rationale: THE PLAYER'S IDEA, 2026-09-08, and the core claim is verified: GALLADE IS THE ONLY POKEMON IN CHAMPIONS THAT LEARNS IMPRISON + PROTECT + WIDE GUARD - 1 of 308 forms. Imprison's real mechanic comes from smogon_basics, not Serebii ('no foe can use any move known by the user'), so carrying those moves denies them to both opponents. THE MOVES MUST ACTUALLY BE IN THE SET for the seal to apply, which is why three slots are forced. COVERAGE, measured over the 394 Worlds Masters teams with a full moveset: 288 of them (73.1%) have NO protective move other than Protect and/or Wide Guard, so Gallade shuts their protection off completely. Every single team carries something - 0 have none. What leaks is DETECT (86 teams, 21.8%), which Gallade cannot learn, plus Baneful Bunker 8.1% and Spiky Shield 2.0%. CLOSE COMBAT IS THE FOURTH SLOT AND IT DOES DOUBLE DUTY: STAB off Atk 125, and it seals the most used Fighting move in the format - 212 slots, 53.8% of teams, against Low Kick's 33% and Focus Blast's 10.7%. Sealing it matters because Mega Glalie is Ice, Fighting x2.
builds.sp_reasoning: 66/66. FINAL, after the player corrected the whole approach on 2026-09-08. Two earlier spreads were wrong for the same underlying reason: they measured Gallade in a state it only occupies for two turns. THE GAME PLAN DEFINES THE SPREAD (player): turn 1 Gallade installs IMPRISON and takes hits; turn 2 Gallade PROTECTS while Glalie Explodes, so it takes nothing; from turn 3 it chooses between CLOSE COMBAT and WIDE GUARD. THEREFORE THE ONLY DEFENSIVE REQUIREMENT IS: NOTHING MAY OHKO A FRESH GALLADE ON TURN 1. Two-turn and three-turn survival numbers are irrelevant, because turn 2 is Protect. WHY A DEFENSIVE INVESTMENT IS A TRAP HERE. Close Combat drops the user's own Def AND SpD by one stage each, every time. Measured on the previous 32-Def spread: after ONE Close Combat, Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave goes 3HKO -> 2HKO, Garchomp's Earthquake 3HKO -> 2HKO, Sneasler's Dire Claw 3HKO -> 2HKO, Brave Bird 2HKO -> 44% OHKO and Flare Blitz 2HKO -> 28% OHKO. After two it is OHKOed by nearly everything. The 32 Def bought numbers that stop being true the moment Gallade starts doing its job. THE MINIMUM WAS MEASURED, NOT GUESSED. With Coba Berry, 32 SP of bulk is enough that NOTHING in the threat panel can OHKO a fresh Gallade - Brave Bird, Dual Wingbeat, Flare Blitz, Last Respects at 50 and 100 BP, Kowtow Cleave, Flower Trick, Moonblast, Shadow Ball, Hurricane. That frees 34 points, and the per-stat cap of 32 sends them to Attack. HP 16 OVER SPD 18, and this is the quiet one: CLOSE COMBAT DROPS DEF AND SPD BUT NEVER HP. HP is the only defensive stat that survives the self-debuff. Both 16/8/10 and 8/8/18 clear turn 1, but after one Close Combat the HP version holds Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave to a 46% OHKO against the SpD version's 75%. ATK 32 WITH ADAMANT, which is what the freed points buy. Against the previous Impish build it gains six lines, four of them real category changes: FLOETTE 3HKO -> 2HKO (27.4% of teams), SNEASLER 3HKO -> 2HKO (26.4%), STARAPTOR 2HKO -> 46% OHKO (17.0%), ARCHALUDON 90% -> GUARANTEED OHKO (10.9%), AERODACTYL 46% -> 97% OHKO (9.9%), GRIMMSNARL 2HKO -> 47% OHKO (8.6%). Kingambit, Incineroar, Tyranitar, Excadrill and Arcanine-Hisui stay OHKOs and Garchomp stays a 2HKO. SPA 0 AND SPE 0. SpA is dead weight on an Atk 125 / SpA 65 Pokemon with no special move, which is what makes Adamant free. Speed is 0 because Steadfast is luck, not a plan - see ability_reasoning. REJECTED SPREADS, all measured: neutral 8/16/16/18/8 (a neutral nature is never right when one stat is dead weight); Impish 8/16/32/10 (the 32 Def evaporates after one Close Combat); Impish 8/32/8/18 (survives turn 1 identically but loses all six offensive lines above).
builds.ability_reasoning: STEADFAST, and it is treated as a LUCKY BONUS, NOT A PLAN (player, 2026-09-08): 'es una habilidad de suerte, por lo que speed no es tan importante'. That is why Speed is 0. An earlier version of this build spent 8-24 SP chasing the post-proc speed tier; that was weighting a coin flip as if it were a guarantee. UNBOOSTED, Gallade at 0 SP is Speed 100 and beats only 3.0% of the field, so the points are worth far more in Def and Atk. When the proc does happen it is pure upside - 100 -> 150 takes it past 58.3% of the field by usage, including Kingambit, Incineroar, Sinistcha and Basculegion. It is still the right ability of the three. SHARPNESS is dead - CLOSE COMBAT IS NOT A SLICING MOVE (flags: Contact, Metronome, Mirror, Protect). JUSTIFIED works mechanically, with no super-effective clause, so Kingambit's Dark moves would trigger it at 52.8% of teams - but the player's read holds: an opponent holding Flying, Ghost or Fairy will not attack a Psychic/Fighting target with neutral Dark. Fake Out on 59.2% of Worlds Masters teams is the most likely trigger.

It is not yet in inventory.items, and the shop price of a berry is NOT recorded anywhere - do not invent one. NOTE FOR THE TEAM SHEET: under the Item Clause this reserves Coba Berry for Gallade, so no other Pokemon on the same six can hold it. STARAPTOR'S BRAVE BIRD OHKOes Gallade at 32 HP / 32 DEF WITH NO BERRY (114-135%); Coba is the only thing in the game that answers it, and it takes it to a 2HKO. KASIB BERRY WAS MEASURED AND REJECTED even though Ghost is the more common threat type (46.2% of teams carry a lethal Ghost attack against 39.6% for Flying). Two reasons: Kasib leaves Brave Bird a guaranteed OHKO on all eight spreads tested, and Last Respects is at its WEAKEST exactly when this plan runs - it is 50 BP until something faints, and the Imprison line resolves on turns 1-2. Coba already gives a 2HKO at 50 BP. Kasib buys safety in a late game this plan never reaches. UNFIXABLE RESIDUAL: Floette's Light of Ruin is a guaranteed OHKO through either berry, on 27.3% of Worlds teams. No spread survives it. SECOND CONSTRAINT, and it is the one that shapes the whole spread: CLOSE COMBAT DROPS GALLADE'S OWN DEF AND SPD BY ONE STAGE EACH, every use. So defensive SP is worth full value for exactly two turns and decays from there, while Attack SP never decays. THIS IS WHY THE BUILD IS NOT DEFENSIVE: buy the minimum bulk that survives turn 1, then put everything else into damage. COBA BERRY IS PART OF THAT MINIMUM - without it Brave Bird OHKOes and no amount of SP fixes it, so the berry is what makes the cheap defensive block possible in the first place. Wide Guard and Protect are the moves to fall back on, and both are high-priority so they still work once Gallade is slow and frail.

builds.turn_1_survival: MEASURED HONESTLY, and the answer is NOT a guarantee - the player asked directly and was told so before spending any VP. AGAINST ONE ATTACK, on this spread with Coba, Gallade survives 12 of the 13 threats measured: Staraptor Brave Bird 79-93%, Incineroar Flare Blitz 76-91%, Gholdengo Shadow Ball 73-87%, Floette Moonblast 84-99%, Meowscarada Flower Trick 65-77%, Whimsicott Moonblast 62-73%, Kingambit Kowtow Cleave 61-72%, Sneasler Dire Claw 55-66%, Garchomp Earthquake 53-62%, Aerodactyl Dual Wingbeat 49-58%, Basculegion Last Respects 32-38%, Sylveon Hyper Voice 18-21%. THE ONE EXCEPTION IS FLOETTE'S LIGHT OF RUIN at 122-145%, a guaranteed OHKO, on 27.4% of Worlds teams. It was tested against Coba, Kasib and up to 32 HP / 32 Def and kills through all of them. That hole is structural, not a spread problem. AGAINST TWO ATTACKS IN ONE TURN this spread survives only 10 of 78 pairs. A full search was run over every nature and every HP/Def/SpD allocation: THE BEST POSSIBLE IS COBA + IMPISH + 32 HP / 32 DEF / 2 SPD, which survives 42 of 78 - and THE PLAYER REJECTED IT 2026-09-09, keeping Adamant. The reasoning is sound and is recorded so it is not re-opened: those 42 pairs are almost all physical+physical, because 32 Def with Impish leaves SpD at 2, so every pair containing a special attacker still kills - and the special half of the field is huge (Floette 27.4%, Sylveon 24.9%, Whimsicott 24.1%). No pair containing Light of Ruin survives in ANY of the configurations tested. So max bulk buys protection against the half of the meta that was hitting softer anyway, and pays for it with seven offensive lines - everything except Kingambit and Incineroar, which fall to type effectiveness regardless. THE REAL ANSWER IS POSITIONING, NOT SP. Do not lead Gallade into a full field on turn 1 if it can be helped; bring it when one threat remains, which turns 78 pairs into 13 single attacks, 12 of which it survives. Never tell the player this build is safe on turn 1 - it is not, and no build is.
